display.text: The occurrence of one or more successes across trials; its complement is no successes. For n independent trials with success probability p, its probability is 1 − (1 − p)ⁿ.
Events for which knowing whether one occurred changes the probability of the other.
Events that cannot occur together, so P(A and B) = 0. Two disjoint events with positive probabilities are dependent. Also called mutually exclusive events.
Events for which learning that one occurred does not change the probability of the other; equivalently, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B).
The event containing outcomes in both A and B; P(A and B) is the probability that both events occur.
For independent events, the probability that all occur is the product of their probabilities; for two, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B).
Returning a selected item before the next random draw, restoring the original composition and probabilities of the sampling pool.
